data.narrative:
Electric Sheep, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Singh, Herold, and Murty, has raised $25.5M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine peers—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private firms spanning seed to Series B, including Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $25.5M raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding $51M. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.1B to $2.0B; the median valuation across this set is $1.6B. The wide spread reflects heterogeneity in stage maturity and market positioning within the robotics sector.

The triangulated range spans $43M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $850M. This wide bandwidth reflects substantial uncertainty inherent in early-stage robotics valuations, where peer comparables span multiple stages and absolute differences in capital deployment and revenue traction remain poorly constrained. The stage-progression method yields a more conservative floor given reliance on historical capital raised, while peer multiples incorporate forward-looking market expectations. Key uncertainties include Electric Sheep's product-stage maturity relative to Series B cohorts and addressable market definition within manufacturing automation.
